title: Forwarding Factories (Shallow Constructors)
pattern: Standalone functions or methods that do nothing but call a public constructor with the exact same arguments.
why_bad: Adds a redundant, shallow naming layer over standard construction, forcing maintainers to trace where the session is created.
detection: A factory function whose signature matches the struct fields and whose body is exactly a direct, unadorned struct construction.
counterexample: Constructors that enforce invariants, select variants of an enum, or hide complex private initialization details.
fix: Remove the factory function and let callers construct the struct directly (or implement `Default`/`new`).
source: Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004), Chapter 6 ("Creation"), p. 57.
